guide.title: Whitemane's Overview
guide.text:
Whitemane is a Healer who can heal her allies with
Zeal by damaging her enemies. She is capable of
trading damage favourably against most Heroes, and must do so in order to
maximise her healing. If she is able to consistently deal damage, she can
generate immense healing for her team.

guide.title: Whitemane's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
High burst healing
Access to a cleanse effect
Weaknesses
Very poor waveclear and Camp clear
Lack of mobility
Healing output largely dependent on damage dealt, therefore low out-of-combat healing
No crowd control
Weak to healing reduction effects

guide.title: Whitemane's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Whitemane synergizes with
Whitemane has synergy with Heroes who can create a lot of space
(for example Johanna) or that like to take prolonged team fights
(such as Sonya) as she can keep healing them for long.
Due to the high amount of raw healing she has access to, Whitemane
is great when paired with Heroes who have Armor
baseline (like Garrosh) or with high uptime
(notably Cassia).
Whitemane is countered by
Whitemane has very limited mobility, and must remain within the threat range
of enemies in order to deal damage to heal her allies. She will struggle
against Heroes who can displace her,
as she lacks any kind of escape once
caught, or crowd control her to death.
Heroes who can deal damage to Whitemane and her teammates
while she cannot damage them back (for example Chromie)
may be difficult to play against. Additionally, Heroes who can significantly reduce or
prevent healing received (such as Deckard Cain with Sapphire
at Level 7) can greatly reduce the effectiveness of Zeal during teamfights.

guide.title: Whitemane's Maps
guide.text:

Whitemane's weaker maps
Whitemane excels in short team fights and at contesting Objectives
that take less than 30 seconds to be secured (for example Infernal Shrines).
If the fight takes too long, she struggles to keep up with her Mana consumption.
The least interesting Maps to play Whitemane on are the ones
where she cannot abuse her kit around the Objective,
that are heavily focused on Mercenaries (such as Sky Temple),
or where the early game is too important (notably Braxis Holdout).

guide.title: Whitemane's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
Desperate Plea is the only Ability in Whitemane's kit that has a Mana cost, but you have to manage your Mana wisely because of the Desperation mechanic.
Use Inquisition immediately after casting Searing Lash to maximise your damage output while they are Slowed.
Cast Searing Lash when you can hit enemy Heroes, preferably when they are under crowd control effects that impair their movements.
Scarlet Aegis can be used during team fights to apply Zeal to multiple allied Heroes without having to pay Desperation cost, given they are in range.
Divine Reckoning should be preferably used as a follow-up to allied crowd control effects that can keep enemy Heroes in place.
Make sure to apply Zeal to allied Heroes before using your Abilities to deal damage, otherwise you will not convert that damage into healing.
When there are no enemy Heroes in range, make sure to use Clemency to sustain your team with out-of-combat healing.
To save Mana, try to use either Inquisition or Clemency to remove 1 Desperation stack before casting Desperate Plea again.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Whitemane's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
Whitemane excels at relatively quick team fights, during which she can get value
from her burst healing and have time to go back for restoring her Mana.
Among her Talents, she has various tools to save teammates from enemy Heroes
who hard engage, leading the opponents to expose
for getting a kill and then suddenly deny it.
Whitemane needs to be able to deal damage in order to heal optimally, so a
strong frontline is necessary for her to reach peak performance. Her complete
lack of waveclear is another weakness that will limit
the team compositions she can fit into. She must have allies who can generate
enough map pressure to make up for her weak macro.
Although Whitemane has clearly defined weaknesses, she can be powerful in many
team compositions, given they have a strong frontline and plenty of waveclear.

abilities.title: Whitemane's Tips and Tricks
abilities.text:
Desperate Plea is the only Ability in Whitemane's kit that has a Mana cost, but you have to manage your Mana wisely because of the Desperation mechanic.
Use Inquisition immediately after casting Searing Lash to maximise your damage output while they are Slowed.
Cast Searing Lash when you can hit enemy Heroes, preferably when they are under crowd control effects that impair their movements.
Scarlet Aegis can be used during team fights to apply Zeal to multiple allied Heroes without having to pay Desperation cost, given they are in range.
Divine Reckoning should be preferably used as a follow-up to allied crowd control effects that can keep enemy Heroes in place.
Make sure to apply Zeal to allied Heroes before using your Abilities to deal damage, otherwise you will not convert that damage into healing.
When there are no enemy Heroes in range, make sure to use Clemency to sustain your team with out-of-combat healing.
To save Mana, try to use either Inquisition or Clemency to remove 1 Desperation stack before casting Desperate Plea again.

abilities.title: Desperate Plea
abilities.text:
Desperate Plea
(Q)
Whitemane
Mana: 45
Heal an allied Hero for 140 (+4% per level) and gain Desperation for 4 seconds.
Desperation increases Desperate Plea's Mana cost by 40, and stacks up to 3 times.
Current Mana Cost: 45
Desperate Plea is the only Ability in Whitemane's kit that has a Mana cost.
It is also the only Ability in her kit that has no cooldown.
While it does provide a small amount of direct healing, the primary function of
Desperate Plea is to apply Zeal to allies relatively often. The
Desperation mechanic allows you to decide on your own cooldown.
Casting Desperate Plea often with
full Desperation stacks is not sustainable. You should
generally prioritise allies that need Zeal during early fights. A good thing to remember
is that the Zeal buff lasts longer than the Desperation debuff. This means that
with careful management, Zeal can be sustainably applied to several allies at
once.
A good practice to default to is to cast Desperate Plea twice, and then
wait for Desperation to expire before casting it again. While there will be
many situations that require you to improvise outside of this pattern, it is a
good starting point to preserve your Mana for when you need it.
In case of emergency, do not hesitate to use Desperate Plea
several times in a row, regardless of how many Desperation stacks you have.
This way you can save an allied Hero from death at the cost of having to use
your Healing Fountain or your Hearthstone to get Mana before the next team fight,
which does not give Experience to the enemy team and is faster than waiting for
an allied Hero to respawn in the late game.

abilities.title: Inquisition
abilities.text:
Inquisition
(W)
Whitemane
Cooldown: 12 seconds
Channel on an enemy Hero for up to 3 seconds, dealing 50 (+4% per level) damage every 0.5 seconds and Slowing them by 30%. Removes a stack of Desperation.
Shares a cooldown with Clemency.
Inquisition damages a target enemy Hero, but must
be channeled. This means that it will lock Whitemane in place unless it is
cancelled or interrupted. You should choose wisely when to
start casting this Ability so you can keep channeling it
for longer but you should also not hesitate cancelling it to move in case of danger
or to cast another Ability if needed.
Because Inquisition removes 1 stack of
Desperation, Desperate Plea
should ideally be cast at least once just before channeling it.
This way, you can damage someone and then reapply
Zeal by spending less Mana.
Inquisition may also be used specifically
for the Slow effect. If an enemy
Hero is out of position and your Allies are nearby, reducing their Movement
Speed may help your team secure a kill. Inquisition has a rather long cooldown,
and should be used this way only when allies are likely to complete the
takedown. Inquisition should be primarily used to maximise your healing output
when allies need it.

abilities.title: Searing Lash
abilities.text:
Searing Lash
(E)
Whitemane
Cooldown: 6 seconds
After 0.5 seconds, smite enemies in a straight line for 82 (+4% per level) damage.
If the first strike hits an enemy Hero, a second strike will occur after a short delay.
Repeatable Quest: Hit Heroes with Searing Lash.
Repeatable Quest: Hit 3 Heroes with Basic Attacks.
Reward: Permanently increase Whitemane's maximum Health by 3 and Mana by 2. Heroes hit with the second strike of Searing Lash count as 2 hits.
Searing Lash has a low cooldown, no Mana cost,
and a very short cast animation. It should usually be cast whenever it is
available. It is good to practice casting it all the time, as this will
increase your familiarity with the Ability. Once constant use of Searing Lash
is second nature, it will be easier to do while managing
Desperate Plea's Desperation stacks.
Searing Lash should ideally be on cooldown
right before casting Inquisition
because its cooldown will keep going while you are
busy channeling that.

abilities.title: Scarlet Aegis
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Scarlet Aegis
(R)
Whitemane
Heroic
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Bolster the spirits of nearby allied Heroes, healing them for 300 (+4% per level) and granting them 40 Armor for 4 seconds.
Scarlet Aegis is a fantastic Heroic that heals
all nearby allies, which applies Zeal to them. This means that you can apply
Zeal to all teammates simultaneously without gaining any Desperation stacks.
The armor provided by this Heroic is also very beneficial.

abilities.title: Divine Reckoning
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Divine Reckoning
(R)
Whitemane
Heroic
Cooldown: 75 seconds
After 1 second, consecrate an area for 4 seconds, dealing 50 (+4% per level) damage every 0.5 seconds to enemies inside. 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes is returned as Mana.
Divine Reckoning deals damage over time in an
area. This can be a great way to increase your healing through Zeal. Divine
Reckoning works best in team compositions that can help trap enemies inside the
consecrated area.

abilities.title: Zeal
abilities.text:
Zeal
(D)
Whitemane
Cooldown: 40 seconds
Whitemane's healing Abilities apply Zeal for 8 seconds. Allies with Zeal are healed for 100% of the damage Whitemane deals to Heroes.
Activate to gain 25% Spell Power and lose 15 Armor for 5 seconds. Can be cast while channeling abilities.
Zeal is an extremely powerful buff that can be
applied to Whitemane and her allies. By converting damage into healing,
it allows Whitemane to trade damage
exceptionally well and to heal several members of her team at the same time.
Whitemane's damage-dealing Abilities can and should
be thought of as potential healing, multiplied by the number of allied Heroes
with a Zeal buff on them. Because of this,
it is important to think about how to maximise your damage per second when
playing her. This can be accomplished by casting her damage dealing Abilities
as often as it is safe to do so.
When the enemy team commits to a fight, it
is ideal to have Zeal applied to all allied Heroes who are in combat.
Zeal can be applied to teammates with any healing Whitemane provides that is
not from Zeal itself. This means that
Desperate Plea, Clemency,
and Scarlet Aegis can be used to apply Zeal. Understanding
this is important for Mana management because Desperate Plea
is the only tool Whitemane has that
has any Mana cost limiting its use.
Zeal's active component temporarily increases Whitemane's Spell Power and
reduces her Armor. This can greatly increase Whitemane's healing
and damage done with Abilities for a short
time but will also increase Whitemane's vulnerability to damage taken,
so you should activate it only when not in danger.

abilities.title: Clemency
abilities.text:
Clemency
(1)
Whitemane
Activate to cast Inquisition on an allied Hero, healing them for up to 329 (+4% per level) over 3 seconds while Channeling. Removes a stack of Desperation
Shares a cooldown with Inquisition.
Clemency heals a target allied Hero, but must
be channeled. This means that it will lock Whitemane in place unless it is
cancelled or interrupted. You should choose wisely when to
start casting this Ability so you can keep channeling it
for longer but you should also not hesitate to cancel it to move in case of danger
or to cast another Ability if needed.
Because Clemency removes 1 stack of
Desperation, Desperate Plea
should ideally be cast at least once just before channeling it.
This way, you can heal someone and then reapply
Zeal by spending less Mana.

abilities.title: Baseline Quest
abilities.text:
Whitemane has a Baseline Quest which requires to hit enemy Heroes
with Searing Lash. Every hit increases
your maximum Health by 3 and maximum Mana by 2.
You should not play too much around this Baseline Quest because
Whitemane is perfectly playable without additional Health and Mana.
That said, any additional Health and Mana you gain is good for you.

Zealous Spirit is a tool that helps you manage
your Mana by creating a Zeal buff on yourself that does not generate a stack
of Desperation. This means that you can have 3 recently activated Zeal buffs
with only 2 stacks of Desperation. Another way to think about this is that
the sustainable amount of active Zeal targets is increased from 2 to 3.
?
Saintly Greatstaff
(Level 7)
Whitemane
Enemy Heroes hit by Searing Lash are marked for 3 seconds. Basic Attacks against them deal an additional 55 (+4% per level) Spell damage and remove the mark.
Saintly Greatstaff makes the next Basic Attack
against enemy Heroes recently hit with Searing Lash
deal bonus Spell Damage. Remember that the additional
damage will increase your healing output because of Zeal.
If you issue a Basic Attack command immediately after casting Searing Lash,
you can benefit from this Talent twice with a single cast because that
Basic Attack will consume the first mark before the second mark will be applied.
✔
Intercession
(Level 7)
Whitemane
Cooldown: 75 seconds
Activate to make an ally Unstoppable for 1 second.
Intercession is one of two tools that Whitemane
has that can grant an ally Unstoppable, the other option being
Scarlet Crusade at Level 20.
Pick this Talent against team compositions who have access to
crowd control effects. You should
position in a way that you will not be the first target
because it cannot be self-cast.

talent_pages.title: Level 10 Talents for Whitemane
talent_pages.text:
In this section we discuss when and why to pick a given Heroic Ability.
If you want to read how they work in detail and/or you are looking for some tips on how to use them,
check them out on the Abilities and Strategy page.
✔
Scarlet Aegis
(Level 10)
Whitemane
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Bolster the spirits of nearby allied Heroes, healing them for 300 (+4% per level) and granting them 40 Armor for 4 seconds.
Scarlet Aegis is a strong Heroic Ability that heals all
nearby allies and applies Zeal to them. This means that you can apply Zeal
to all nearby allied Heroes simultaneously without gaining any Desperation stacks.
The bonus Armor provided by this Heroic is also very beneficial, and can counterbalance the
Armor debuff that is caused by activating Zeal.
If you lose 15 Armor and gain 40 Armor, you end up having 25 Armor remaining.
?
Divine Reckoning
(Level 10)
Whitemane
Cooldown: 75 seconds
After 1 second, consecrate an area for 4 seconds, dealing 50 (+4% per level) damage every 0.5 seconds to enemies inside. 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes is returned as Mana.
Divine Reckoning is a good Heroic Ability that deals damage over time in an
area, and restores some Mana based on damage dealt. The damage done by it will
increase your Zeal's healing. Divine Reckoning works best in team
compositions that can help trap enemy Heroes within its area.

talent_pages.title: Level 13 Talents for Whitemane
talent_pages.text:
✔
Subjugation
(Level 13)
Whitemane
Inquisition reduces all damage the target deals by 50%.
Subjugation greatly reduces the damage of any
enemies affected by Inquisition. It pairs extremely well with
Shared Punishment, which can double the number of
affected enemy Heroes.
?
Lashing Out
(Level 13)
Whitemane
If Searing Lash's second strike hits an enemy Hero, reduce its cooldown to 1 second.
Lashing Out allows you to cast Searing Lash much more
often in team fights, as long as the second strike hits an enemy Hero.
While in theory it is a powerful Talent, in practice it will be hard to get value from it,
unless the enemy team has low mobility
and/or your team has a lot of crowd control.
✘
Scarlet Wrath
(Level 13)
Whitemane
Basic Attacks against Heroes increase the duration of all active Zeals by 0.75 seconds, restore 1% Mana to all Zeal targets, and lower the cooldown of Zeals activation by 4 seconds.
Scarlet Wrath is a weak Talent that provides
various effects when Whitemane hits an enemy Hero with Basic Attacks:
extend the duration of all active Zeal buffs by a small amount,
restore a bit of Mana to all allied Heroes who have a Zeal buff on them,
and reduce the cooldown of Zeal.
A prolonged Zeal buff does not need to be refreshed by casting
Desperate Plea that often,
resulting in less Mana consumption during long team fights.
The fact that Basic Attacks on enemy Heroes restore Mana as a percentage
of your maximum Mana means you will gain more Mana when having a lot of stacks
on your Baseline Quest.
We do not recommend this Talent because is does not have any strong synergy with other Talents
and it has low value compared to the alternatives in the same Tier.

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Whitemane
talent_pages.text:
?
Radiance
(Level 16)
Whitemane
Reaching 3 stacks of Desperation heals for 190 (+4% per level) and reapplies Zeal to allies with Zeal.
Radiance is situational Talent that can help Whitemane
heal more than usual, mostly in the form of burst healing,
but also by refreshing the duration of any active Zeal,
which helps when sustain healing is needed.
A common trick is to use Scarlet Aegis to spread Zeal
to make it trigger on as many allied Heroes as possible rather than only on 3 Heroes,
however, you still need to use Desperate Plea to reach
3 stack of Desperation in order to get the healing from Radiance.
A secret trick is to make Radiance trigger
by reaching 3 stacks of Desperation, use Inquisition
or Clemency to remove 1 stack of Desperation,
and make it trigger again by going back to 3 stacks of Desperation.
✔
Shared Punishment
(Level 16)
Whitemane
Upon casting, Inquisition can chain to an additional enemy Hero near its target, dealing 50 (+4% per level) damage every 0.5 seconds. Affected enemies lose 10 Armor.
Shared Punishment increases healing by doubling
the number of Inquisition targets, if two enemy Heroes happen to be close
to each other, and reduces the Armor of enemy Heroes
affected by Inquisition.
Shared Punishment will still cause Inquisition to
chain to an enemy Hero if it is cast onto an allied Hero via Clemency.
This trick enables you to position more safely when you intend to use Inquisition on an enemy Hero
or to reach an enemy Hero that is out of range.
?
Harsh Discipline
(Level 16)
Whitemane
Hitting a Hero with Searing Lash while they are being targeted by Inquisition Roots them for 1.5 seconds.
Passive: Reduce Inquisition's cooldown by 2 seconds.
Harsh Discipline is the only Talent in Whitemane's
kit that can inflict hard crowd-control.
To make the Root happen, you have to cast Searing Lash
and then follow with Inquisition immediately after.
While being a crowd control Talent, Harsh Discipline might indirectly increase
your healing by ensuring that the second strike of Searing Lash
will hit an enemy Hero. The damage produced this way will be converted to healing thanks to
Zeal. All that said, following up
on crowd control by allied Heroes
will give you the same result, unless your team lacks crowd control,
in which case you might like this Talent a bit more.

talent_pages.title: Level 20 Talents for Whitemane
talent_pages.text:
✔
Scarlet Crusade
(Level 20)
Whitemane
Scarlet Aegis heals for 50% more and makes affected allies Unstoppable for 2 seconds.
Scarlet Crusade is a strong Talent that
can grant multiple allied Heroes, and even Whitemane, Unstoppable.
During the late game, preventing or removing
crowd-control Abilities can often mean turning the
game in your team's favor.
?
Judgment Day
(Level 20)
Whitemane
Divine Reckoning deals 50% more damage and pulls enemies to its center the first time it hits them.
Judgment Day is a good upgrade for Divine
Reckoning that adds a bit of crowd-control to the
consecrated area. If your team composition's win condition is to
chain damage dealing Heroics, this may be a good
option.
?
Guiding Light
(Level 20)
Whitemane
Cooldown: 30 seconds
Activate to cast a permanent Zeal on an allied Hero that costs no Mana and doesn't grant Desperation. Only one can be active at a time and has global cast range.
Increases the Spell Power bonus provided by Whitemane's trait by 15%.
Guiding Light is a situational Talent that increases
the Spell Power gained from Zeal's activation
from 25% to 40%. In addition to that, it can be activated to permanently grant
Zeal to an allied Hero.
Thanks to the infinite Zeal's duration
on a single Hero, you may want this Talent if your team has a Hero who likes
to dive (for example Zeratul), however,
the default Zeal duration of 8 seconds is enough in most situations.
The additional Spell Power provided by this Talent when activating
Zeal can be quite useful to heal allied
Heroes for more but it is generally less useful than either
Heroic Ability's upgrade and can barely compete with
Purge the Wicked's offensive uses.
?
Purge the Wicked
(Level 20)
Whitemane
Cooldown: 40 seconds
Activate to blast an enemy Hero with holy fire, reducing their Armor by 25 and dealing 300 (+4% per level) damage over 4 seconds.
Purge the Wicked is a good Talent that can be cast on an enemy Hero
to reduce their Armor and deal damage over time, useful
when your team struggles getting a kill.
Keep in mind that the additional damage
will be converted to healing from your Trait, Zeal,
making it a good option when you require additional healing as well.
